data.name: Alaric
data.long_meaning: From the Germanic elements al (all) and ric (ruler or power). Alaric translates to 'ruler of all'. This name was borne by several early Germanic kings, most notably Alaric I, who ruled the Visigoths from 409 to 410 AD and sacked Rome.

data.cultural_impact: Alaric is most significantly known as the leader who sacked Rome in 410 AD, marking the end of ancient Rome's glory and the beginning of the Middle Ages. His name became synonymous with the fall of the Roman Empire and the shift in political and cultural power from antiquity to the Middle Ages.

Alaric's legacy serves as a reminder that power and authority are not just worldly achievements, but also spiritual callings.

The name Alaric is composed of the Germanic elements al (all) and ric (ruler or power), and translates to 'ruler of all'. Alaric's meaning and origin have significant cultural and religious value, as it represents the power and authority of a ruler in the context of early Germanic and Christian history.
